name: Science
topics: Materials · Eco-home · Safety at home · House design

licoes.texto: A food chain shows how energy passes from one living thing to another. It always starts with the Sun.
pontos: Producers (plants) make their own food with sunlight.
Herbivores eat only plants. Carnivores eat only meat. Omnivores eat both.
Decomposers (fungi and bacteria) break down dead plants and animals.
grass → rabbit → fox
licoes.fala: I eat rice, beans and chicken, so I am an omnivore!

licoes.texto: Each part of a plant has a job.
pontos: Roots take in water and hold the plant in the soil.
Stem carries water up and holds the plant up.
Leaves make food by photosynthesis: sunlight + water + carbon dioxide → food + oxygen.
Flowers make seeds; fruits protect the seeds.
licoes.fala: Plants give us the oxygen we breathe. Thank you, plants!

licoes.texto: A habitat is the home of a living thing. An adaptation is a special feature that helps it survive there.
pontos: Desert: a cactus stores water in its thick stem; a camel can go days without drinking.
Arctic: a polar bear has thick fur and fat to stay warm.
Ocean: fish breathe with gills.
Rainforest: monkeys have long tails and arms to climb trees.
licoes.fala: If a polar bear lived in the desert, it would be way too hot! Every animal fits its habitat.

licoes.texto: A life cycle shows how a living thing is born, grows and makes new living things.
pontos: Butterfly: egg → caterpillar (larva) → chrysalis (pupa) → adult butterfly.
Frog: egg → tadpole → froglet → adult frog.
This big change in body shape is called metamorphosis.
licoes.fala: A tadpole has a tail and lives in water. Later it becomes a frog that jumps on land!

licoes.texto: Matter can be a solid (ice), a liquid (water) or a gas (water vapor).
pontos: Melting: solid → liquid (ice cream melts).
Freezing: liquid → solid (water becomes ice).
Evaporation: liquid → gas (puddles dry in the sun).
Condensation: gas → liquid (drops on a cold glass).
licoes.fala: My ice cream melted in the sun: solid to liquid. Science happens even at snack time!

licoes.texto: Our body has organs that work together in systems.
pontos: Heart: pumps blood around the body.
Lungs: help us breathe (take in oxygen).
Stomach: helps digest food.
Brain: controls the body. The skull protects it.
The skeleton holds us up and protects our organs.
licoes.fala: When I run, my heart beats faster to send more blood to my muscles!

licoes.texto: Microorganisms are living things so small that we need a microscope to see them.
pontos: Bacteria and fungi are examples.
Some are helpful: yeast makes bread rise; bacteria help make yogurt.
Some make us sick: wash your hands with soap and water for 20 seconds!
licoes.fala: Under the microscope, a drop of pond water is full of tiny living things!

questions.q: Which material is transparent, letting light pass through?
questions.fb: O vidro é transparente — por isso é usado nas janelas, deixando a luz natural entrar.

questions.q: Why is brick a good material for walls?
opts: It is strong and lasts a long time
questions.fb: O tijolo é resistente e durável, suportando o peso da construção e protegendo do vento e da chuva.

questions.q: Which property does a roof material most need?
questions.fb: O telhado precisa ser impermeável (waterproof) para a chuva não entrar. Telhas e metal cumprem bem esse papel.

questions.q: What is an adobe brick made of?
opts: Soil (clay), water and straw, dried in the sun
questions.fb: A receita do adobe: terra (argila) + água + palha. Mistura-se, molda-se e deixa secar ao sol até endurecer.

questions.q: Why is straw added to an adobe brick?
opts: To hold the mud together so the brick does not crack
To give it a nice colour
To make it lighter to carry
questions.fb: A palha funciona como “fio” dentro do barro, segurando a mistura e evitando que o tijolo rache ao secar.

questions.q: Which material would be a bad choice for a house in a very rainy place?
questions.fb: A palha absorve água e apodrece com a chuva constante. Por isso casas de palha aparecem mais em climas secos.

questions.q: What do solar panels on a roof do?
questions.fb: Os painéis solares transformam a luz do sol em eletricidade, reduzindo o uso de energia da rede.

questions.q: Why do eco-homes collect rainwater?
opts: Because rainwater is always safe to drink
To reuse it for cleaning, the garden and the toilet, saving water
questions.fb: A água da chuva é guardada e reutilizada em tarefas que não precisam de água potável, economizando água tratada.

questions.q: Which of these makes a house more eco-friendly?
opts: Using recycled materials and big windows for natural light
Leaving all lights on day and night
Using as much water as possible
Building with materials brought from very far away
questions.fb: Materiais reciclados, luz natural, isolamento e materiais locais reduzem o impacto da casa no meio ambiente.

questions.q: Which of these is a dangerous item in a house?
questions.fb: Produtos de limpeza são tóxicos e devem ficar guardados longe do alcance de crianças, sempre nos frascos originais.

questions.q: Which room usually has the most dangerous items?
opts: The kitchen, with knives, the stove and hot pans
questions.fb: A cozinha reúne facas, fogo, panelas quentes e eletricidade — por isso exige mais atenção e supervisão.

questions.q: What should you do to make a house safer?
opts: Leave the floor wet after cleaning
Store knives at the edge of the table
Play near the stove while cooking
Keep medicines and matches out of reach and cover electrical sockets
questions.fb: Guardar remédios e fósforos em lugar alto, proteger tomadas e secar o chão molhado evitam a maior parte dos acidentes domésticos.

questions.q: Which material is flexible (it bends without breaking)?
questions.fb: Rubber (borracha) é flexível. Vidro e tijolo são rígidos e quebram.

questions.q: Which material is the strongest for building tall buildings?
questions.fb: Steel (aço) e concrete (concreto) aguentam muito peso — por isso são usados em arranha-céus.

questions.q: Why is wood a popular building material?
opts: It is light, easy to cut and comes from trees
questions.fb: Leve e fácil de cortar. A desvantagem é que pode queimar e apodrecer com a umidade.

questions.q: What does waterproof mean?
opts: It absorbs a lot of water
questions.fb: Waterproof = à prova d'água. Telhados e capas de chuva precisam dessa propriedade.

questions.q: Which material would you choose for a window?
opts: Glass, because it lets light in
questions.fb: O vidro é transparent e deixa a luz natural entrar.

questions.q: What is a floor plan?
opts: A drawing that shows the rooms of a house seen from above
questions.fb: A floor plan (planta baixa) mostra os cômodos vistos de cima, como um mapa da casa.

questions.q: Why do houses in very rainy places often have steep (sloping) roofs?
opts: So the rain runs off quickly
questions.fb: O telhado inclinado faz a água escorrer rápido, evitando infiltração e o peso da água parada.

questions.q: Why do houses in very hot places often have thick walls and small windows?
questions.fb: Paredes grossas seguram o calor fora e janelas pequenas reduzem a entrada de sol — a casa fica fresca.

questions.q: What should a designer think about first when planning a house?
opts: Who will live there and what they need
questions.fb: Bom design começa pelas pessoas: quantas são, do que precisam e como vão usar os espaços.

questions.q: What does insulation do in a house?
opts: Keeps heat inside in winter and outside in summer
questions.fb: O insulation (isolamento) nas paredes e no telhado reduz a perda de calor — a casa gasta menos energia.

questions.q: Why is it good to use local materials to build a house?
opts: They do not need to travel far, so less fuel and pollution
questions.fb: Materiais locais percorrem menos distância, gastando menos combustível no transporte.

questions.q: What does recycled material mean?
opts: Material that cannot be used again
Material made from things that were used before
questions.fb: Reciclado = feito a partir de algo já usado, poupando recursos naturais.

questions.q: Which room has the highest risk of slipping?
opts: The bathroom, because the floor gets wet
questions.fb: O banheiro molhado é onde mais se escorrega. Tapete antiderrapante ajuda muito.

questions.q: What should you do if you see a broken electrical wire?
opts: Do not touch it and tell an adult
questions.fb: Nunca toque — eletricidade é perigosa. Avise sempre um adulto.

questions.q: Why should medicines be kept locked away?
opts: Because they look nice in a box
Because small children could take them by mistake
questions.fb: Remédios parecem balas para uma criança pequena. Guardar em lugar alto e trancado evita acidentes graves.
